text:
sam: Heads-up — the sample edge worker is failing with our JS SDK when using generic overloads + bundler. Types blow up in the worker build, but not in Node dev. Anyone seen this? :facepalm:

anna-l: Ugh. Is this the tsserver error or the bundler/rollup/esbuild step? Usually NodeNext vs Classic resolution trips folks up.

sam: It fails at build-time in CI (esbuild target=es2020 -> edge). Local tsc ok. Error in the emitted d.ts referencing 'unknown' from a generic overload: 

sam: ```
error TS2742: 'Redwood' is exported but uses name 'unknown' from external module "@types/some-lib" which cannot be named.
at node_modules/@redwood/sdk/index.d.ts:14:25
```

kai: That smells like a conditional types + exported generics issue combined with isolatedModules or declaration emit. For edge builds we transpile to ESM and use NodeNext resolution. Two quick things: set "skipLibCheck": true and ensure "moduleResolution": "NodeNext". Also check "declaration": true vs false for your bundler.

maria: Also worth checking "esModuleInterop" + "allowSyntheticDefaultImports" — bundlers sometimes rewrite imports which changes type emission. For Edge worker samples we enforce: 

maria: ```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "isolatedModules": true
  }
}
```

anna-l: If isolatedModules is true, you can't use const enums or certain type-only value patterns; it can break how overloads are inferred. For the SDK we recently shipped a fix to avoid re-exporting anonymous conditional types in the root d.ts — but older SDKs still hit this. Which SDK version is the sample using?

sam: Using @redwood/sdk v0.12.3 (pinned in sample). I can try bumping. CI log attached: 

build-bot: ```
> yarn workspace sample build
> esbuild src/worker.ts --bundle --format=esm --target=es2020 --outfile=dist/worker.js
TS ERROR: node_modules/@redwood/sdk/index.d.ts:14:25: error TS2742: Exported variable 'Redwood' has or is using name 'unknown' from external module "@types/some-lib" but cannot be named.
Failed with exit code 2
```

kai: If bumping the SDK isn't an option, a narrower workaround is to add a small patch to the sample's types: create a local d.ts shim that imports the problematic type under a name and re-exports it explicitly so the emitter can name it. Ugly but works. Example: 

kai: ```ts
// types/shim.d.ts
import type { Problematic } from '@types/some-lib';
export type NamedProblematic = Problematic;
```

maria: Another route — adjust package.json conditional exports for the bundle to point to an ESM-typed entry and a CJS-typed entry so the emitter picks the right typedefs. Example: 

maria: ```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```

sam: Sweet. Any recommendation for a minimal default tsconfig we should add to the sample repo so new users don't hit this?

anna-l: Yes — add an "edge-sample" tsconfig in the repo root and extend it in the sample: 

anna-l: ```json
{
  "extends": "../tsconfig.edge.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "composite": false,
    "declaration": false
  }
}
```

sam: I'll try bumping SDK first, then shim if needed. If this is a common pain, we should add a one-liner in the quickstart about "if you hit TS2742 -> try these tsconfig flags or bump SDK".

maria: Agreed. I'll open a tiny PR to add a troubleshooting blurb + the tsconfig file. Thanks for the repro, sam — saved me time. :thumbsup:
